question: Client assets per advisor across the five -- and is that comparison even valid?

claims.text: Edward Jones - the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states the Partnership ended 2025 with client assets under care (AUC) of $2.5 trillion, including $1.1 trillion of advisory programs AUC, and with 20,425 financial advisors.

Edward Jones - the 10-Q for the period ended 2026-03-27 (published 2026-05-07) states the Partnership ended the first quarter of 2026 with $2.4 trillion of AUC and 20,550 financial advisors. The table shows total client AUC at period end of $2,417 billion.

Raymond James - the FY2025 10-K (period 2025-09-30, published 2025-11-25) states that total client assets under administration (AUA) in the Private Client Group segment were $1.67 trillion, of which $1.01 trillion was fee-based AUA. It states 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors were affiliated with the firm at that date.

Comparability - each firm reports assets on its own basis, and the evidence does not put them on one definition. Edward Jones uses 'assets under care'. Raymond James uses PCG segment 'client assets under administration', with advisors counted across employee and independent contractor channels. Morgan Stanley separates 'advisor-led client assets' (accounts with a Wealth Management representative assigned) from self-directed assets. Schwab reports firm-wide total client assets. The reporting dates also differ (Edward Jones and Raymond James at 2025 year-end or fiscal year-end, others in 2026).

adjacent.text: Bank of America's GWIM investor-day deck (published 2025-11-05) shows $4.6T of client balances and more than 15K wealth advisors for 'Merrill | Private Bank'. The 10-Q for 2026-03-31 reports GWIM client balances of $4.6 trillion.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley - the 10-Q for 2026-03-31 reports Wealth Management advisor-led client assets of $5,784 (2025 comparison: $5,715) and fee-based client assets of $2,792. The Q3 2026 call (published 2026-10-14) cites $10.5 trillion of total client assets across Wealth and Investment Management.
adjacent.differs_because: No advisor count appears in the evidence for Morgan Stanley. The $10.5 trillion also covers Investment Management as well as Wealth Management, so it is not advisor-attached assets.

adjacent.text: Schwab - the 3Q26 press release (published 2026-10-15) shows total client assets of $13,333.2 billion, split into Investor Services $7,487.3 billion and Advisor Services $5,845.9 billion.
adjacent.differs_because: These are firm-wide custodial and brokerage assets, including RIA custody and self-directed clients. No employed-advisor count is given, so they are not assets per advisor.

gaps.what: Client assets per advisor is not disclosed as a reported metric by any of the five firms in the evidence, and a ratio cannot be built on a like-for-like basis. Only Edward Jones and Raymond James have both an asset figure and an advisor count on their own definitions.
gaps.suggested_source: Each firm's 10-K or 10-Q advisor-count and client-asset tables, restated to a common definition and date, or an industry study that normalizes assets per advisor.

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America supplemental GWIM disclosures; Merrill-only figures would have to come from a firm statement.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - financial advisor headcount not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley 10-K or earnings supplement (Wealth Management financial advisor count).

gaps.what: Schwab - an advisor count comparable to the others is not found in the evidence provided. Schwab's client assets are mostly custodial and self-directed.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab 10-K / monthly activity report (Wealth Advisory and Advisor Services metrics).
